_comment: HANGING PROTOCOLS: how a case is laid out the moment it opens, and what that
arrangement is CALLED.
WHAT THIS IS BUILT ON, AND WHAT IT IS NOT BUILT UNDER. MOS-UI-209 says a case MUST
open with its series already laid out, under a NAMED hanging protocol, and that 'the
reader MUST NOT have to find the series, choose between them, or construct the
layout'. That sentence is the whole of why this file exists.
The rest of MOS-UI-209 is about a product that is gone: the protocol 'MUST be
contributed as a hangingProtocolModule from the extension package and MUST be named in
ohif.lock', and MOS-UI-213 binds every requirement in 19.4.4 to 'OHIF configuration or
a module contributed from the extension package'. OHIF was withdrawn at specification
0.4.0; there is no extension package loaded and no ohif.lock. So 19.4.4 does not reach
this surface, exactly as 19.4.4's MOS-UI-211 does not reach src/image/mpr.js -- see
that file's header for the same argument made once already, including the correction
of an earlier version of it that claimed the requirement DID reach it.
The substance is built anyway, because it is right, and it is recorded here as
substance rather than as compliance. MOS-UI-209 remains UNMET as written: it selects a
protocol by the annotation campaign's capability_id, and the clinical viewer has no
campaign.
A PROTOCOL IS NAMED ON SCREEN. That is not decoration either. An arrangement that
appears without saying why teaches a reader that the layout is arbitrary, and the day
it puts the scout in panel one they will assume it always did. The name is in the left
rail, and it says 'overridden' the moment the reader picks a layout themselves --
because after that the screen is theirs and the protocol is no longer describing it.
THE FALLBACK IS DECLARED, NOT IMPLICIT. The last entry has an empty `when` and
therefore always matches. A table whose last rule can fail is a table that sometimes
arranges nothing while claiming to have arranged something.
WHAT `when` CAN ASK, and nothing else -- an unknown key makes a rule NOT match rather
than match vacuously, so a typo loses its own rule instead of silently catching every
study:
priorOpen       true when more than one study is on screen
modality        every image series in the study carries this modality
minImageSeries  at least this many CT/MR/PT series
maxImageSeries  at most this many
